title: Set the level

brief.story: The bench thermostat compares the temperature sensor with a set point from a knob. The set point is a potentiometer across 9 V: its wiper can sit at any voltage from 0 to 9 V.
brief.goal: Turn RV1’s knob so its wiper (column 6) sits at 5.2–5.6 V.

hints: Across the supply, a potentiometer is a voltage divider you can adjust: the wiper splits the track into a top part and a bottom part.
The track from leg 1 to the wiper is the top resistor (10 kΩ × position), the rest is the bottom. V_wiper = 9 V × bottom ÷ 10 kΩ.
For 5.4 V the bottom part needs 5.4 ÷ 9 = 60 % of the track, so the knob goes to 40 %.

spec.label: Wiper voltage
spec.explain: The wiper divides the track: V = 9 V × (track below the wiper) ÷ (whole track).

debrief: Across a supply, a potentiometer is an adjustable voltage divider: the wiper picks any voltage between its two ends. Set points, volume controls, joysticks and the trimmers on sensor boards all work this way, and a microcontroller reads the wiper to know where the knob is.
